title: Segment report pair
description: A segment's pair of reports: what its provider says it sent, and what the provider of the route's next segment says it received, each about its own segment and with the receipt of the stated entry holding its statement, and the sending party's tuple's terms they are compared under: its fill increment and its gross or net convention (REQ-ORD-9, REQ-CAT-11). The last segment of a route has no pair. That the two are different parties', that the pair's segment is the sent report's and the received report's another, and that a gross figure's charge is no more than it, are checked by the Rust types; that the received segment is the route's next, and each party its segment's provider, by the log's citation table.

segment.description: The segment whose end the pair compares: its sent report's.

received.description: What the receiving party reports, about the route's next segment after the sent one.

terms.description: The sending party's tuple's terms, which orchestration fills from them where it builds the pair (REQ-CAT-11, ADR-0009).

report.description: One party's report about its own segment.

party.description: The provider that reports: its statement's maker (acts), so two adjacent providers of one publisher report a pair (REQ-ORD-9), and the provider the log moved its segment's value with.

segment.description: The segment the report is about, which its statement's about names: the sent report's is the pair's segment, the received report's the route's next segment after it (T-020-38).

amount.description: The amount, in the asset's unit.

statement.description: The receipt of the stated entry that holds the party's statement.

terms.description: What the comparison reads of the sending party's tuple: two reports less than one increment apart raise nothing, and a gross figure is compared net of its charge.

increment.description: The tuple's fill increment, in the reports' unit; absent where the tuple declares none, and the reports are then compared exactly.

reported_as.description: Whether the sending party's figure is gross or net of its charge.

charge.description: The charge the figure holds, in the reports' unit, which the comparison takes off it; no more than the amount sent. A conversion's charge is in an asset it doesn't give out, so 0.
